ownership_reason: Only the gold divides the two parts of the fraction and decides, from the float quotient it has just computed, whether both parts must first be brought into the float range; hops 1-4 pass the numerator and the denominator along unchanged and return the gold's float, and once the gold has returned NaN the value of the fraction cannot be recovered from it. The gold's javadoc promises the value of the fraction as a float, which for (10^401 + 1) / (2 * 10^400) is 5, not NaN. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the sibling BigFraction.doubleValue, intact beside the facade, replaces a NaN quotient of the double values by the quotient of both parts shifted right by the larger bit length minus Double.MAX_EXPONENT, and BigFractionTest testDoubleValueForLargeNumeratorAndDenominator, which asserts 5 for the same fraction, passes; BigFraction.bigDecimalValue computes the value of a fraction from its parts whatever their size (testBigDecimalValue passes); testFloatValue and testDoubleValue pin the ordinary quotients. Shifting both parts in a caller before the gold is a second implementation of the gold's own rescaling step: applied unconditionally it changes the fraction handed to the gold for every input and, for a numerator far larger than the denominator (2^200 / 3), hands the gold a zero denominator, which the documentation of every hop and of the gold excludes.
